require 'sinatra'
require 'json'
require 'securerandom'
require 'openssl'
require 'base64'

set :sessions, false

MASTER_KEY = ENV.fetch('MASTER_KEY') { SecureRandom.hex(32) }
USERS_DB = {}
TOKENS = {}

module Auth
  ROLES = { 'viewer' => 1, 'editor' => 2, 'admin' => 3 }.freeze

  # Derive a fixed 32-byte key with full entropy regardless of input length.
  def self.derived_key
    OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.digest(MASTER_KEY)
  end

  def self.role_level(role)
    ROLES[role] || 0
  end

  def self.has_permission?(user_role, required_level)
    user_level = role_level(user_role)
    user_level >= required_level
  end

  def self.generate_token(user_id, role)
    payload = { 'uid' => user_id, 'role' => role, 'iat' => Time.now.to_i, 'exp' => Time.now.to_i + 3600 }
    raw = JSON.generate(payload)
    cipher = OpenSSL::Cipher::AES.new(256, :GCM)
    cipher.encrypt
    cipher.key = derived_key
    iv = cipher.random_iv
    cipher.auth_data = 'token'
    encrypted = cipher.update(raw) + cipher.final
    tag = cipher.auth_tag
    Base64.urlsafe_encode64(iv + tag + encrypted, padding: false)
  end

  def self.verify_token(token_str)
    return nil unless token_str
    raw = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(token_str)
    iv = raw[0, 12]
    tag = raw[12, 16]
    ciphertext = raw[28..]
    decipher = OpenSSL::Cipher::AES.new(256, :GCM)
    decipher.decrypt
    decipher.key = derived_key
    decipher.iv = iv
    decipher.auth_tag = tag
    decipher.auth_data = 'token'
    plaintext = decipher.update(ciphertext) + decipher.final
    payload = JSON.parse(plaintext)
    return nil if payload['exp'].to_i < Time.now.to_i
    payload
  rescue
    nil
  end
end

module AccessControl
  # Check if the request meets the minimum role requirement
  # required_level can come from route configuration
  def self.authorize!(token_payload, required_level)
    return false unless token_payload
    user_role = token_payload['role']
    # Support both string role names and numeric levels from config
    effective_requirement = normalize_requirement(required_level)
    Auth.has_permission?(user_role, effective_requirement)
  end

  def self.normalize_requirement(level)
    case level
    when String
      Auth.role_level(level)
    when Integer
      level
    else
      level.to_i
    end
  end
end

# Route protection configuration
ROUTE_PERMISSIONS = {
  'GET /documents' => 'viewer',
  'POST /documents' => 'editor', 
  'DELETE /documents' => 'admin',
  'GET /admin/users' => 'admin',
  'POST /admin/users' => 'admin',
  'PUT /admin/config' => 'admin'
}

before do
  content_type :json
  @token = nil
  auth_header = request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']
  if auth_header&.start_with?('Bearer ')
    token_str = auth_header[7..]
    @token = Auth.verify_token(token_str)
  end
end

helpers do
  def require_auth!(min_role = nil)
    halt 401, JSON.generate({error: 'unauthorized'}) unless @token
    if min_role
      route_key = "#{request.request_method} #{request.path_info}"
      # Use route-specific permission if defined, otherwise use the parameter
      configured_level = ROUTE_PERMISSIONS[route_key] || min_role
      unless AccessControl.authorize!(@token, configured_level)
        halt 403, JSON.generate({error: 'forbidden'})
      end
    end
  end

  def current_user_id
    @token&.dig('uid')
  end
end

post '/auth/register' do
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  username = data['username'].to_s.strip
  password = data['password'].to_s
  halt 400, JSON.generate({error: 'invalid input'}) if username.empty? || password.length < 8
  halt 409, JSON.generate({error: 'exists'}) if USERS_DB[username]
  salt = SecureRandom.hex(16)
  hashed = OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(password, salt, 100_000, 32, 'sha256')
  USERS_DB[username] = { password_hash: hashed, salt: salt, role: 'viewer', id: SecureRandom.uuid }
  JSON.generate({status: 'created', role: 'viewer'})
end

post '/auth/login' do
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  username = data['username'].to_s
  password = data['password'].to_s
  user = USERS_DB[username]
  halt 401, JSON.generate({error: 'invalid credentials'}) unless user
  computed = OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(password, user[:salt], 100_000, 32, 'sha256')
  unless OpenSSL.secure_compare(computed, user[:password_hash])
    halt 401, JSON.generate({error: 'invalid credentials'})
  end
  token = Auth.generate_token(user[:id], user[:role])
  JSON.generate({token: token, role: user[:role]})
end

# Admin endpoint to promote users
post '/admin/users' do
  require_auth!('admin')
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  target = data['username'].to_s
  new_role = data['role'].to_s
  halt 400, JSON.generate({error: 'invalid role'}) unless Auth::ROLES.key?(new_role)
  user = USERS_DB[target]
  halt 404, JSON.generate({error: 'not found'}) unless user
  user[:role] = new_role
  JSON.generate({status: 'updated', username: target, role: new_role})
end

get '/documents' do

end

post '/documents' do

# The critical endpoint - delete requires admin
delete '/documents' do
  require_auth!('admin')
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  JSON.generate({status: 'deleted', id: data['id']})
end

# Admin config endpoint
put '/admin/config' do
  require_auth!('admin')
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  JSON.generate({status: 'config_updated'})
end

# User profile - any authenticated user
get '/profile' do
  require_auth!
  JSON.generate({uid: @token['uid'], role: @token['role']})
end

# Batch operations endpoint - processes multiple actions
post '/batch' do
  require_auth!('viewer')
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  results = []
  actions = data['actions'] || []
  actions.each do |action|
    op = action['operation'].to_s
    resource = action['resource'].to_s
    # Determine required permission for each sub-action
    perm_key = "#{op.upcase} /#{resource}"
    required = ROUTE_PERMISSIONS[perm_key]
    # If no specific permission found, deny the action
    if required.nil?
      results << { op: op, status: 'denied', note: 'unknown_operation' }
    else
      if AccessControl.authorize!(@token, required)
        results << { op: op, status: 'executed' }
      else
        results << { op: op, status: 'denied' }
      end
    end
  end
  JSON.generate({results: results})
end
